items.t: Waymo pauses all robotaxi rides on U.S. freeways after California ban
items.d: Waymo will stop putting its driverless vehicles on U.S. freeways for now.
items.fullText: U.S. news Waymo pauses all robotaxi rides on U.S. freeways after California ban The state ban was imposed after a pair of incidents near San Francisco, officials said. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 California bans Waymo vehicles from freeways 01:26 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 17, 2026, 6:24 PM EST / Updated Nov. 18, 2026, 2:51 AM EST By Tim Stelloh , Lindsay Good and Joe Kottke Waymo will stop putting its driverless vehicles on U.S. freeways for now. The move comes after California banned the company’s robotaxis from state highways after officials determined that they pose an “imminent hazard to public safety.” “We’ve proactively implemented a freeway operating restriction across all of our markets,” a Waymo spokesperson said Tuesday in a statement. “Notably, this only extends to our freeway service, and we’re working to quickly and safely re-open freeway routing.” California’s Department of Motor Vehicles said it issued its ban Nov. 11 after one of Waymo’s autonomous vehicles tried to pass highway patrol officers conducting a traffic break on a San Francisco-area freeway this month. The department also cited a separate incident in which three of the company’s vehicles entered an active construction closure on another San Francisco-area highway. A Waymo robotaxi drives in North Beach on July 07, 2026 in San Francisco. Heather Diehl / Getty “The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,” the department said. Similar restrictions were placed on the company after similar incidents earlier this year, the department said. items.fullText: Korea Advances Physical AI Across Industries With NVIDIA November 8, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Tapping into the country’s strengths in manufacturing and engineering, NVIDIA is helping advance Korea’s physical AI ecosystem. The country’s industry leaders are applying accelerated computing, AI and simulation to everything from semiconductor manufacturing to robotics and autonomous vehicles. These efforts are helping bring physical AI from development into real-world production. Samsung Advances Semiconductor Engineering With Accelerated Computing and AI Physics Samsung Electronics is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA to advance semiconductor innovation through accelerated computing and AI physics. The work spans materials research, process development and device engineering. In technology computer-aided design, Samsung is working with NVIDIA cuISS and NVIDIA cuDSS to accelerate computations involving sparse linear systems. The collaboration also extends to GPU acceleration for process and optical simulations. In materials research, Samsung’s sMOL platform has run selected quantum chemical calculations up to 5x faster end to end with NVIDIA cuEST . Samsung is also exploring NVIDIA cuEquivariance to speed up tensor operations used in training and inference for atomistic AI models. Samsung is developing chip-scale thermal and mechanical analysis workflows with NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo . In one AI homogenization case, combining AI-predicted effective material properties, coarser grids and GPU acceleration resulted in a roughly 1,600x speedup. Simulation time fell from about 18 hours for a fine-grid solve on a 32-core CPU to 41 seconds for a GPU-accelerated coarse-grid solve. Looking ahead, NVIDIA Agent Toolkit could connect these simulation tools and AI models, helping future engineering agents run analyses and compare design options.
